verdicts.reading: Closed spectral polygons are shape, open ones are motion: random boosts move the dominant scallop biphase by 3.6e-15 deg while the mirror flips it exactly, and the bulk skewness/asymmetry are closed-triad sums to machine precision.  On the real scallops the parity breaking is dynamic, not stored: the flux quadrature is decisive (t = -4.7) while the shape asymmetry is weak (0.17 +- 0.25, t = 2.4) with an unstable biphase (30 deg, frame circ-std 47 deg) -- the same frames that migrate decisively (NR49).  Migration and flux parity live at the pair level, invisible to every closed polygon; strong Im B (dunes) would certify asymmetric nonlinear coupling, which these scallops barely have.
